reader_cross_check.question: is the decoder's parcel-outline reconstruction faithful to the app's stored post-interaction boundary pieces, or is the refusal a decode-fidelity issue?
reader_cross_check.site_container_topology: BOTH files' site containers are AECC_FEATURE_STYLE records (Labels-Parcels 0x4676, Parcel-2C 0xC38) whose topology graph does NOT decode: the walk passes elevation_keys, elements and the 0x80000001 gate, but node_list reads 0 NODES (the moved-members form) and the edges walk then refuses. The app's stored split pieces (lot lines + faces) are therefore NOT readable on parcel sites with the current grammar — a READ gap (topology.rs node_list/edges; the reader was validated on feature-line/grading containers, Grading-3A et al., never on parcel sites)
reader_cross_check.what_is_stored: the per-record proxy-graphics rings decode 54/54 and 11/11 as closed rings; rings share edges/vertices with neighbours (Labels-Parcels 208/1431 parcel pairs, Parcel-2C 19/55), and the app stores the shared pieces ONCE (54 parcels vs 55 lot lines; 11 vs 30) — per-record rings drawn through shared coordinates ARE the post-interaction boundaries
reader_cross_check.verdict: the READER's ring reconstruction is faithful to what each parcel record stores; the residual does NOT live on the ring-decode side. The refusal lives on the WRITER side's REPRESENTATION: it injects each ring as an INDEPENDENT closed lot line, duplicating the shared boundary pieces, which the site's topology correctly refuses to meet. (Reader-side nuisance found en route: Parcel-2C parcel records store EMPTY names — the app reads 'ROAD (LOCAL): 100' et al. via the style's name template; parcel_name() also evaluates to no name in this probe — flagged, not blocking, separately dispatchable)
